column1: # Every setting Nebula reads, and which settings app offers it. tools/settings_table.py --check compares this table with
# the engine's readers (render_config.cpp, runtime_settings.cpp, input_bindings.cpp), the Windows launcher
# (installer/src/Launcher), the Android launcher (platform/android/app) and the game's own menu (runtime/src/ui), and
# exits 1 on any difference. Linux has no separate app: its settings app is the game's menu (the game column).
# key       the key in its file; tune.*.<name> is one per control scheme, bind.*.* every binding
# file      config (config.ini), runtime (runtime_settings.ini), android (the Android app's "controls" preferences)
# field     the C++ member that holds it (RenderConfig, RuntimeSettings, RuntimeAudioSettings, SchemeTuning); - none
# type      bool, int, float, enum, set, text, state (written by the game for itself, never offered)
# values    bool 0|1; enum the file's names, the n-th name stored as n; set the allowed numbers; int and float lo..hi/step
# default   the engine's default when the key is absent (apple= on Apple's systems; scheme: per control scheme)
# page      the page a settings app shows it on: Display, Graphics, Audio, Controls, General, Performance; - not offered
#           y offered; n missing (an open defect); s shown as a status only; - not on that platform or not a setting
# capability when an app offers it (an app hides it, never shows a choice the device cannot run)
# label     the English name (the launchers' text row in localization/NebulaText.tsv; the game's menu shows it in capitals)
